claims.text: The material is a PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst.
Intergranular boride precipitation can be introduced into the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst as a controlled structural change.
Intergranular boride precipitation enhances grain-boundary cohesion in the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion modifies reactant transport during ethanol oxidation.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion modifies product transport during ethanol oxidation.
The transport modifications caused by enhanced grain-boundary cohesion improve ethanol-oxidation catalytic activity.
The transport modifications caused by enhanced grain-boundary cohesion improve ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
A catalyst containing intergranular boride precipitates will have higher catalytic activity than an otherwise comparable catalyst without those precipitates.
A catalyst containing intergranular boride precipitates will have improved selectivity relative to an otherwise comparable catalyst without those precipitates.
The appropriate baseline is a PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst without intergranular boride precipitation.
The proposed comparison is intended to apply under ethanol-oxidation reaction conditions.
Failure of boride precipitation to improve both measured activity and selectivity relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
